rounds.text: Meesho Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and profit expansion that significantly outpaces the broader market, evidenced by a 30% compounded sales growth over 3 years and a 34% growth in the trailing twelve months [E13, E14], alongside a 49% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16]. This commercial momentum is backed by powerful institutional accumulation, with foreign institutions increasing holdings by 5.53 percentage points and domestic institutions adding 8.32 percentage points, driving a positive institutional money flow change of +9.11 percentage points [E32, E33, E34]. The market is rewarding this operational trajectory, pushing the stock to 93% of its 52-week range while remaining above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages in a classic bull configuration, complemented by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E35, E37, E38]. Furthermore, the company operates with a pristine balance sheet featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x and is classified as almost debt-free, which reduces financial risk while it capitalises on a Consumer Services sector tailwind score of +0.57 [E27, E44, E59]. Operational efficiency is also starting to turn a corner, with the quarterly operating margin improving by 5 percentage points to -6% in June 2026 compared to the same period a year ago [E20]. Conceded: the company trades at a rich price-to-book multiple of 24.04x and exhibits negative return on equity metrics alongside negative operating cash flows [E1, E8, E24].

The stock trades at an exorbitant price-to-book ratio of 24.04x on a book value of ₹ 9.61 [E1], or 24.52x against a sector benchmark of just 2.28x [E6], while sitting near its 52-week high [E36] with an annualised volatility of 57.0% [E40]. This rich valuation completely ignores severe fundamental deterioration, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of -46.2% [E12], a 3-year median ROE of -63% [E17], and a negative return on capital employed of -40.0% [E11]. Operating profitability remains deeply troubled as operating margins sit at -11% in the trailing twelve months with an inconsistent trajectory [E19, E21], producing a terrible P/E of -89.5x compared to the sector benchmark of 26.12x [E5]. Furthermore, the business is burning massive amounts of cash, reporting a staggering operating cash flow of Rs -3,875 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -3,976 Cr for March 2026 [E24, E25]. Conceded: compounded sales growth stands at 34% in the trailing twelve months [E14] alongside positive institutional money flows [E34].

The bear points to an exorbitant price-to-book ratio of 24.04x and high volatility [E1, E40], but this ignores the powerful underlying momentum driving the stock near its 52-week high with a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 [E35, E38]. Conceded: the business has a negative return on capital employed and terrible historical ROE [E11, E17], yet the company is almost debt free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E27, E44]. While operating margins and cash flows have been strained [E19, E24], the quarterly operating margin showed a meaningful 5 percentage point improvement in June 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E20]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on past profitability completely discounts explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including 34% trailing twelve-month sales growth and a 49% compounded profit growth over the same period [E14, E16]. This operational acceleration has triggered massive institutional buying with a positive money flow and a holding change increase of 9.11 percentage points [E34], alongside a strong sector tailwind in Consumer Services [E59].

The bull leans heavily on near-52-week-high momentum and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E35, E38], but a rich price-to-book multiple of 24.04x combined with an annualised volatility of 57.0% means the entry price already discounts all the good news and leaves investors exposed to severe downside [E1, E40, E56]. Conceded: the company carries almost no debt with a ratio of 0.01x [E27], yet this conservative financing sits atop a deeply insolvent operational reality featuring a disastrous 3-year median ROE of -63% and a TTM ROE of -46.2% [E12, E17]. While the bull highlights a single quarterly margin tick-up in June 2026 [E20], the broader yearly trend is flagged as inconsistent, and TTM operating margins actually worsened by 5 percentage points over three years [E19, E21]. Furthermore, despite top-line and profit growth figures [E14, E16], the business bled massive cash with operating and free cash flows crashing to Rs -3,875 Cr and Rs -3,976 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E24, E25]. Finally, while institutional inflows increased [E34], low promoter holdings of just 16.34% signal weak insider alignment while the fundamental score remains dragged down by decelerating earnings and low historical returns [E31, E47, E54].
